#1.Basic R Operations
# Addition
10 + 5

# Subtraction
10 - 5

# Multiplication
10 * 5

# Division
10 / 5

# Exponentiation
2^3

# Square root
sqrt(25)
# Numeric vector
age <- c(20, 35, 32, 29)

# Display the vector
age

# Calculate the average age
mean(age)

# Calculate the summary
summary(age)
# Character vector
names <- c("Aline", "Rose", "Eric", "Jean")

# Logical vector
results <- c(TRUE, FALSE, TRUE, TRUE)

# Integer vector
numbers <- 9:29

# Display the vectors
names
results
numbers
#Factors
A factor is a data structure used to store categorical variables. Factors are useful when working with data that contains different categories or groups.
# Create a gender factor
gender <- factor(c("Male", "Female", "Male",
                   "Female", "Female"))

# Display the factor
gender

# Display the levels
levels(gender)

# Count observations in each category
table(gender)

# Check the structure
str(gender)
# Create an ordered factor
education <- factor(
  c("Primary", "University", "Secondary",
    "University", "Primary"),
  levels = c("Primary", "Secondary", "University"),
  ordered = TRUE
)

# Display the factor
education

# Check the levels
levels(education)
#Create a matrix
A matrix is a two-dimensional data structure that stores elements of the same data type in rows and columns.
# Create a matrix
marks <- matrix(
  c(75, 80, 85, 90, 70, 95),
  nrow = 2,
  ncol = 3
)

# Display the matrix
marks

# Display the dimensions
dim(marks)

# Display the number of rows
nrow(marks)

# Display the number of columns
ncol(marks)
#Access elements in a matrix
# Access the first row
marks[1, ]

# Access the second column
marks[, 2]

# Access the element in row 1, column 2
marks[1, 2]

# Calculate the total of all marks
sum(marks)
#Create a list
A list is a data structure that can store different types of elements, including numbers, characters, vectors, and other data structures.
# Create a student list

student <- list(
  Name = "Marie",
  Age = 25,
  Marks = c(75, 85, 90),
  Passed = TRUE
)

# Display the list
student

# Display the structure
str(student)
#Access elements in a list
# Access the student's name
student$Name

# Access the student's age
student$Age

# Access examination marks
student$Marks

# Calculate average marks
mean(student$Marks)

# Access the first element
student[[1]]
#Create a data frame
# Create a student data frame

students <- data.frame(
  StudentID = c(1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6),
  Name = c("Aline", "Rose", "Eric", "Jean", "Marie", "Peter"),
  Age = c(22, 24, 21, 23, 25, 26),
  Gender = c("Female", "Female", "Male",
             "Male", "Female", "Male"),
  Marks = c(75, 85, 68, 90, 80, 72)
)

# Display the dataset
students
#Explore the data frame
# Display the first six rows
head(students)

# Display the last six rows
tail(students)

# Display the structure
str(students)

# Generate descriptive summary
summary(students)

# Check the dimensions
dim(students)

# Display column names
names(students)

# Count the number of rows
nrow(students)

# Count the number of columns
ncol(students)
#Select columns from a data frame
# Select the Name column
students$Name

# Select Name and Marks columns
students[, c("Name", "Marks")]

# Select the first three columns
students[, 1:3]
# Filter rows
# Select students who scored 80 or above

high_performers <- students[students$Marks >= 80, ]

# Display the result
high_performers\
#Add a new column
students$Status <- ifelse(
  students$Marks >= 50,
  "Pass",
  "Fail"
)

# Display updated dataset
students
# Calculate average marks
mean(students$Marks)

# Calculate highest marks
max(students$Marks)

# Calculate lowest marks
min(students$Marks)

# Calculate standard deviation
sd(students$Marks)
#Practise using dplyr
packa
library(dplyr)
# Select specific columns
students %>%
  select(Name, Marks)

# Filter students with marks above 75
students %>%
  filter(Marks > 75)

# Arrange students from highest to lowest marks
students %>%
  arrange(desc(Marks))

# Calculate average marks
students %>%
  summarise(Average_Marks = mean(Marks))
  students %>%
  filter(Marks > 75) %>%
  arrange(desc(Marks))
#Missing Values in R
# Create a dataset with missing values
students_missing <- data.frame(
  StudentID = 1:6,
  Name = c("Aline", "Rose", "Eric", "Jean", "Marie", "Peter"),
  Age = c(22, NA, 21, 23, NA, 26),
  Marks = c(75, 85, NA, 90, 80, NA)
)

# Display the dataset
students_missing
#Identify missing values
is.na(students_missing)
#Count missing values
# Count all missing values
sum(is.na(students_missing))

# Count missing values in each column
colSums(is.na(students_missing))
